title: Reading Aśokan edicts: a first session in Brāhmī
subtitle: Live online lecture with a guided reading of the Girnar rock edict
description:
A two-hour live session that takes you from the Brāhmī alphabet to reading a full line of an Aśokan edict by yourself. We cover how the script was deciphered, the sound values of each letter, and the conventions epigraphists use when they publish a reading.

You get the handout and the estampage images a day before the session. The recording stays available to registered participants for 30 days.
speaker: Talaash Heritage faculty

title: Understanding the Śākta ethos from the Devīmāhātmya
subtitle: Lecture recording on the tantric tradition
description:
The full recording of our lecture on how the Devīmāhātmya frames the Goddess, and what that tells us about the Śākta and tantric traditions that grew around the text.

Watch at your own pace. The reading list and slides are included.
speaker: Talaash Heritage faculty

details.Access: Link on your order page after payment

title: One-to-one counselling: studying and working in archaeology and heritage
subtitle: A 45-minute video call about your next step
description:
A private conversation about where you are and where you want to go: which MA or PhD programmes suit you, how entrance exams and fieldwork applications work, what jobs exist in museums, surveys, conservation and heritage management, and what to do in the next six months.

Send your questions and your CV beforehand so the time is spent on answers. You get a written summary of the advice after the call.
speaker: Talaash Heritage faculty

details.Booking: Choose your time from the calendar link on your order page after payment
details.Rescheduling: Free up to 24 hours before your slot

title: Indian temple architecture: Nāgara, Drāviḍa and Vesara
subtitle: Six-week weekend course
description:
Six Saturday sessions that teach you to read a temple: its plan, its elevation and the vocabulary used to describe both. By the end you can look at a śikhara or a vimāna and place it by region and period.

Each week has one live class, one reading and a short identification exercise with feedback.
speaker: Talaash Heritage faculty

details.Certificate: On completing four of six exercises

title: Mehrauli Archaeological Park: a thousand years in three hours
subtitle: Guided heritage walk in Delhi
description:
A morning walk through Mehrauli, from the stepwells to the tombs, with an archaeologist who shows you how to tell a Sultanate arch from a Mughal one and why the difference matters.

Groups are kept small so everyone can hear and ask questions. Wear walking shoes and carry water.
speaker: Talaash Heritage faculty

title: Harappan gallery up close: a museum morning with an archaeologist
subtitle: Small-group experience at the National Museum, New Delhi
description:
Three hours in one gallery instead of thirty minutes in ten. We look at seals, weights, beads and pottery the way an excavator does: what it is made of, how it was found, and what it can and cannot tell us.

You leave with a short illustrated guide to the objects we discussed.
speaker: Talaash Heritage faculty

details.Museum entry: Not included; buy at the counter

title: Brāhmī script chart
subtitle: A3 print with Devanāgarī and roman equivalents
description: Every Aśokan Brāhmī letter with its Devanāgarī and IAST equivalent, set large enough to read from across a room. Printed on 250 gsm matte paper and shipped rolled in a tube.

title: Trench notebook
subtitle: Gridded field notebook with a printed scale on the cover edge
description: A pocket notebook built for site visits: 5 mm grid pages for plans and sections, a 15 cm scale printed along the cover edge, and a stitched spine that lies flat.

title: Twelve monuments postcard set
subtitle: Measured drawings of twelve Indian monuments
description: Twelve postcards, each with a measured elevation drawing on the front and a short note on the back about when the monument was built and what to look for when you visit.

title: Harappan seals reading pack
subtitle: Printed booklet with a recorded introduction
description: A 48-page booklet on how Harappan seals were made, used and excavated, with drawings of forty seals at actual size. Comes with a one-hour recorded introduction you can watch before you read.
